query: Frost in the Chalk The cellar goes cold. The lanterns shrink. A girl in white furs steps into the chalk and frost creeps out from her boots across the flagstones: Ilse Dumont. "They said the academy's best come down here," she says. She looks you over. "They lied. But you'll do." Fight her She slips on her own ice and your spell catches her before she's up. She stays down a moment, then laughs, a short Northern sound. "Again," she says. "Not tonight. But again." She takes her purse and leaves the cellar colder. Rime closes over your wand hand and you can't feel it to cast. She stands over you, unimpressed. "You fight like someone taught you," she says. "Find someone who didn't." Your fingers ache till morning. Ask her why she's down here She doesn't answer. Instead she tells you your stance is wrong, then fixes it, roughly, with her boot. "Southerners," she says, as if that explained everything. The crowd boos you both, and she doesn't seem to hear.

results.title: Frost on the Door
results.excerpt:
Frost on the Door
Your door is sealed in ice, a hand thick, clear as glass. Someone has scratched a word into the frost: a Northern word you don't know. It doesn't sound kind. In the village, they say, a girl in white furs bought nothing today, and smiled.

results.title: Frost on the Inside
results.excerpt:
Frost on the Inside
Winter has got into the dormitories. The windows frost over on the inside every night, and the warming ward the professors put up keeps cracking. Everyone is sleeping in their coats, and the porters say it will be mended next week, as they said last week.
